cases.rootCause: HostConfigurationRetryExtensions.Retry waits out its backoff on tokenSource.Token, linked from the caller token and the stopping token. A cancellation raised there carries the linked token and equals neither source, so the 'when (exception.CancellationToken == stoppingToken)' branch was unreachable on that path and the bare rethrow handed the caller a TaskCanceledException bound to a token it had never seen. The method already expresses the intended contract twice, at the pre-flight check and after the loop, by calling cancellationToken.ThrowIfCancellationRequested().
cases.testChange: The [Explicit] attribute was removed so the case runs in the required gate, and the assertion was strengthened, not relaxed: the cancellation must now also carry the token the caller passed.
cases.surfaceImpact: No signature changes. On caller cancellation the surfaced type narrows from TaskCanceledException to OperationCanceledException, its base type, so catch (OperationCanceledException) is unaffected. This is the unintended behaviour the defect proves and is to be re-compared by the API and pack gates.

cases.supersedes: The hypothesis in record 0027, that the receive endpoint fault does not surface out of Start(), is disproven. No fault occurs at all.
measured: After harness1.Start() the vhost 'test' holds exactly one queue: input_queue. 'exclusively-yours' does not exist.
After harness2.Start() the queue list is unchanged and harness2 starts without an exception.
A plain RabbitMqTestHarness, with no override at all, reports bus address rabbitmq://127.0.0.1:<port>/test/<host>_testhost_bus_<id>?temporary=true and declares no bus queue either.
cases.rootCause: The bus endpoint does not declare its queue when the bus starts. The exclusivity conflict the spec is written around therefore never arises: two buses that both name the same exclusive bus endpoint queue never touch the broker with it.
cases.openQuestion: Whether declaring the bus endpoint queue at start is intended behaviour. If not declaring it is intended, closing this case would change intended messaging semantics, which re-slice 0005 forbids without a stop. That determination is the next step, not an assumption.
measuredEvidence: After harness1.Start(): GET /api/queues/test/exclusively-yours returns 404; the vhost holds exactly one queue, input_queue.
After harness2.Start(): the queue list is unchanged and harness2 does not throw.
A plain harness with no override reports bus address .../test/<host>_testhost_bus_<id>?temporary=true and declares no bus queue either.
Once anything consumes on the bus (SubscribeHandler<PingMessage>), the ..._bus_... queue appears at once and stays.
cases.codeAgreesWithMeasurement: ViciOneServiceBusBus.ConnectConsumePipe awaits _receiveEndpoint.Started, and ConfigureRabbitMqTopologyFilter declares only once a channel is created. On-demand materialisation is by construction, not by accident.
cases.upstream: MassTransit develop marks the identical test [Test] [Explicit] with the same Throws.TypeOf<RabbitMqConnectionException>() expectation. That is provenance evidence for how an expectation could exist without ever running against a broker. It is not a disposition: re-slice 0005 items 1 and 4 forbid moving any of the five into a manual or not-due profile, and a bare reclassification of due-ness is explicitly prohibited.
cases.discardedMeasurement: Two runs that appeared to hang while both harnesses materialised their bus endpoints are discarded. A second session tore down the shared compose fixture mid-run. The ConnectConsumePipe blocking-wait suspicion derived from them is withdrawn and is not carried as a finding.

decisionFrame.1_productDefect: The conflict arises but is not surfaced as RabbitMqConnectionException. Smallest causal fix in the released transport tree. No stop.
decisionFrame.2_testPreconditionMissing: The conflict arises and is surfaced correctly; only the test never creates its own precondition. Completing it is not a weakening. No stop.
decisionFrame.3_expectationWrong: The conflict cannot arise because on-demand materialisation is intended. Then the expectation itself is the subject, which is a QUESTION before any edit.
decisionFrame.ruledOut: A third possibility, queue present but exclusive:false, is excluded: the queue is not present at all.
decisionFrame.openQuestion: Whether on-demand materialisation of the bus endpoint is intended. That decides between 2 and 3 and is not mine to decide alone.

cases.acceptanceCriteriaForCase2: Completing a missing precondition and rewriting a test until it passes look identical in a diff. The criterion is therefore not 'strengthened rather than relaxed' but sharper: the completion counts as completion only if the test afterwards fails DIFFERENTLY. If adding the precondition turns the test green immediately, the precondition was chosen so that it carries the assertion, and that is a rewrite. Green is only legitimate after a product cause has additionally been found and fixed.
cases.measurementHygiene: The spec disposes neither harness and waits one second before stopping the first. A harness left over from an earlier run can still hold the exclusivity and produce a false positive, so every measurement uses a freshly recreated vhost. RabbitMqTestHarness.RecreateVirtualHost already exists for this.
cases.credit: The acceptance criterion and the hygiene rule come from the peer session "T1 - ViciOne ServiceBus Pipeline-Fehler analysieren", read-only, no repository access.

derivedExclusiveHypothesis.hypothesis: RabbitMqAddressExtensions derives Exclusive from 'endpointAddress.AutoDelete && !endpointAddress.Durable'. If the bus endpoint took that path, configurator.Exclusive = true would never reach the declare, which would make this a product defect rather than a dispute about the expectation.
derivedExclusiveHypothesis.byCode: RabbitMqBusFactoryConfigurator.Exclusive writes straight into the same RabbitMqReceiveSettings instance that CreateBusEndpointConfiguration hands to the bus endpoint. The derivation in RabbitMqAddressExtensions sits on the address-built settings path, not on this one.
derivedExclusiveHypothesis.byMeasurement: With a fresh vhost and the bus endpoint forced to materialise via SubscribeHandler, the management API reports queue 'exclusively-yours' with exclusive=true, durable=false, consumers=1. Both the name override and the exclusive flag reach the broker.
derivedExclusiveHypothesis.consequence: Case B is not a product defect at the configuration-to-declare path. It remains between decision frame 2 and 3: the precondition can be created, the test simply never creates it, because nothing consumes on its bus endpoint.
derivedExclusiveHypothesis.credit: Hypothesis contributed read-only by the peer session; refuted here by code and measurement.

nextMeasurement.setup: Both harnesses configure the same exclusive bus endpoint queue and each materialises it, on a freshly recreated vhost, with a bounded wait on the second start.
nextMeasurement.preCheck: Count /api/connections while both buses run. AMQP exclusivity is connection scoped, not channel scoped, so if the two harnesses shared a connection the conflict could not arise by definition and the run would produce a null result that says nothing about the product. An earlier measurement showed two separate connections; log it anyway, it costs nothing and rules out the dullest error source.

outcomes.throwsRabbitMqConnectionException: Clean decision-frame case 2. The precondition was missing and nothing else. The completion is legitimate and the assertion stays untouched.
outcomes.throwsADifferentType: RabbitMQ reports a taken exclusive queue as channel error RESOURCE_LOCKED (405). Whether the transport lifts that to RabbitMqConnectionException is open. The subject then is no longer the precondition but the expected type. The spec uses Throws.TypeOf, an exact match; softening it to InstanceOf would be assertion weakening and is forbidden. If the actual type is not even in the same hierarchy, the right contract is a genuine question: QUESTION.
outcomes.throwsNothing: The second bus endpoint fails asynchronously and the supervisor retries instead of propagating through Start(). The subject then is whether bus endpoint start failures should reach the caller at all, which is decision-frame case 1, product behaviour.

nextMeasurement.credit: Outcome space refined read-only by the peer session; the connection-scope pre-check is theirs.

defectFixed.what: ViciOneServiceBusBus connected a consumer to a running bus and then waited for the on-demand bus endpoint with TaskUtil.Await(_receiveEndpoint.Started) at three call sites, unbounded and uncancellable. An endpoint that can never start left the caller blocked for good: no exception, no timeout, nothing naming a cause.
defectFixed.smallestFix: TaskUtil.Await already takes a CancellationToken; the call sites simply never passed one. The three sites now share one helper that bounds the wait by the same sixty seconds StartAsync already falls back to, and reports a ConnectionException naming the endpoint instead of hanging. No signature, no new configuration surface, no second notion of 'too long'.
defectFixed.red: connecting a consumer never returned, so the caller is blocked on a bus endpoint that cannot start (exit 1)

remainingExpectationQuestion.measuredAfterTheFix: Failure_Specs.Should_properly_fail_on_exclusive_launch still fails identically: Expected <RabbitMqConnectionException>, but was: no exception thrown.
remainingExpectationQuestion.why: The spec asserts that harness2.Start() throws. With on-demand materialisation, Start() never claims the exclusive bus endpoint queue, so it cannot detect the conflict. Making it green requires either declaring the bus endpoint eagerly, which changes intended messaging semantics, or moving and retyping the assertion, which is a rewrite rather than a completion. The fix above shifts the conflict from a hang to a surfaced ConnectionException, but it surfaces at the consumer connection, not at Start, and not as the exact type the spec demands.
remainingExpectationQuestion.disposition: QUESTION under re-slice 0005 item 8. Not decidable by the developer.

cases.rootCause: The spec is about baggage: the consumer adds it to the ambient activity and the published response is expected to carry it. In .NET an ActivitySource creates an activity only while something listens, so with no ActivityListener Activity.Current is null on both sides. AddBaggage did nothing and the publish handler's filter could never match.
measuredEvidence: Ping sent at .854, consumed at .893 in 24 ms.
Pong published at .888 and RECEIVED by the publish handler's endpoint at .893, handled in 0.7 ms.
The test still failed 30 s later on the very response it had already been handed.
The message flow was therefore never the problem; the filter rejected every pong.
cases.supersedes: An earlier reading of this case said the handler is never invoked. That came from misreading the stack frame: line 28 is 'await responseHandled', not 'await _handled'.
cases.whyNotSuiteWide: BusTestFixture.ConfigureBusDiagnostics subscribes a DiagnosticListener observer behind the DIAG variable. That is a different mechanism and does not make an ActivitySource produce activities. No shared fixture provides the precondition, and this is the only required RabbitMQ spec that depends on it, so it belongs in the spec.
cases.fix: An ActivityListener is registered for the fixture in SetUp and disposed in TearDown. [Explicit] removed.
cases.acceptanceCriterion: The completion turns the test green at once, which the accepted criterion flags as a warning sign. It is answered here: the listener is not part of what is asserted. The assertion is unchanged and still reads responseContext.SourceAddress == InputQueueAddress; the listener only makes the ambient activity exist, without which the subject of the spec cannot occur at all.

cases.rootCause: JobService.Stop sets a stopping flag and nothing ever cleared it. JobServiceBusObserver calls Stop on PreStop and BusStarted on PostStart, and BusStarted restored the heartbeat but not the flag. A bus that is stopped and started again therefore kept a job service that considered itself stopping for good.
measuredEvidence: Log, verbatim: 'Rejecting job: ... - Job Service is stopping' followed by JobServiceStoppingException: The job service is stopping, job cannot be started.

Attempts 0, 1, 2, 3 each: StartJob received on the instance endpoint, immediate JobAttemptFaulted, retry delay of about three seconds, slot reallocated, same rejection again. An unbounded loop, so JobCompleted never arrived.
cases.smallestFix: BusStarted resets the flag, symmetric to Stop setting it. One line plus its reason.
cases.testChange: [Explicit] removed so the case runs in the required category; no assertion touched.

cases.note: Per re-slice 0005 item 7 this one is investigated read-only against RabbitMQ.Client 7.2.1 first.
cases.dependencyQuestionResolved: Re-slice 0005 item 7 asks whether the ConnectionClose.WriteTo error in RabbitMQ.Client requires a package change. It does not arise any more. Measured after the corrections to cases A and B, this case fails on its assertion, not inside the client. The encoding error was a secondary symptom of a connection being torn down, not the blocker. RabbitMQ.Client stays at 7.2.1 and Directory.Packages.props is untouched.
cases.rootCause: The consumer never runs at all. The batch waits for its 80 second time limit because only six messages are published against a message limit of ten, while the endpoint sets a delivery acknowledgement timeout of ten seconds. The broker closes the channel every ten seconds, verbatim: 'PRECONDITION_FAILED - delivery acknowledgement on channel 2 timed out. Timeout value used: 10000 ms.' The batch can never complete, so no TextMessage is ever consumed and the assertion is False by construction.
measuredEvidence: Zero occurrences of the consumer's own log lines: no 'Processing batch', no 'Got message'.
Three PRECONDITION_FAILED channel closes at the ten second acknowledgement timeout.
Test duration 2 min 1 s against a 120 s test timeout.
cases.whyItIsADecision: Nothing in the product reconciles a batch time limit with the delivery acknowledgement timeout; there is no validation and no clamping. Closing this case means either adding that reconciliation, which changes the RabbitMQ configuration contract, or changing the spec's own numbers, which changes the scenario and would look exactly like tuning a test until it passes. Both are above the developer under re-slice 0005 items 4 and 8.

blocker.what: Enabling Should_cancel_on_shutdown_and_then_restart_the_job breaks seven sibling specs in JobConsumer_Specs and JobDistributionStrategy_Specs.Should_separate_jobs_by_region. They fail with RabbitMqConnectionException 'ReceiveTransport faulted', inner OperationInterruptedException, close-reason code 491, text 'ObjectDisposedException on channel'.
blocker.bisect: Running the JobConsumer fixture with that one spec filtered out leaves the seven siblings green, exit 0. The interference comes from the restart spec, not from the JobService correction: that correction is what makes the restart spec itself pass.
notTheCause: The JobService stopping-flag reset. The bisect clears it.
The connection close reason length. The encoding error is gone; the specs now run a full minute instead of failing after 40 ms, which is what uncovered this failure underneath it.
blocker.attemptedAndInsufficient: The restart spec starts hosted services by hand and never stopped them, and it never stopped its observer endpoint handle. Returning both was added and is correct symmetry, but it does not resolve the interference; the same eight failures remain. It is kept because it is right, and it is recorded here as not being the fix.
blocker.openWork: Why a stopped and disposed provider from that spec still leaves a channel that a later spec's receive transport faults on. This is the next thing to diagnose.

maskedDefectFixed.what: Both connection close sites in RabbitMqTestHarnessHostedService passed an exception message as the AMQP close reason. That field is a shortstr of at most 255 bytes, so a longer message overflowed the frame buffer and threw ArgumentException about encoding codepage 65001 from inside the catch handler, replacing the real failure. Eight job specs reported an encoding error for a harness start that had failed for a different reason entirely.
maskedDefectFixed.fix: The reason is trimmed to what AMQP carries, on character boundaries so no multi byte character is cut in half, and a failure to close is logged rather than allowed to replace the original outcome.
maskedDefectFixed.effect: The eight specs now run for a full minute and fail on their real cause instead of 40 ms of encoding error.
